[open] Issue #796: P2: Panel silently swallows malformed arbiter responses — empty choices treated as cache miss
  Author: @anchapin
  Status: OPEN
  URL: https://github.com/anchapin/nexus-proxy/issues/796

  Description:
    ## P2: Panel silently swallows malformed arbiter responses
    
    **Focus area**: D — Upstream & Cascade
    **PRD phase**: Phase 2 — Observability & Metrics
    **Estimated effort**: S (1 day)
    **Labels**: bug, area:upstream, phase:2-observability
    
    ### Problem
    In `Panel` at `upstream.go:628-659`, if the arbiter returns a **valid HTTP 200 with valid JSON but `choices` is empty or missing**, `fetchErr == nil` and `synthesis == ""`. The function returns `false, nil` — which tells the caller "cache miss, arbiter was invoked" — but the response written to `w` is an empty-content completion. The caller increments `nexus_fusion_arbiter_cache_total{reason="cache_miss"}` **incorrectly** because the arbiter was called but returned garbage.
    
    ### Proposed solution
    When `synthesis == ""` after parsing, treat it as an error: return `false, fmt.Errorf("fusion: arbiter returned empty synthesis")` rather than falling through to `writeCachedArbiterJSON`. This ensures `cacheHit=false` is always paired with either a successful arbiter response or an error, never with silent empty-content writing.
    
    ### Acceptance criteria
    - [ ] `TestPanel_MalformedArbiterEmptyChoices_ReturnsError` — mock arbiter returning `{"choices": []}`, assert non-nil error and `cacheHit == false`
    - [ ] `TestPanel_ValidArbiterResponse_ReturnsNoError` — mock arbiter returning valid synthesis, assert nil error, `cacheHit == false`
    - [ ] `TestPanel_CacheHit_ReturnsNoError` — mock arbiter cache hit, assert nil error, `cacheHit == true`
    - [ ] `make test-race` passes
    
    ### References
    - `internal/upstream/upstream.go:634-659` — the silent-fallthrough code path

# Nexus Proxy Makefile
#
# Common development tasks. CI runs `make ci` which gates on vet, build,
# test, and lint. Everything else is convenience for local iteration.

GO          ?= go
BINARY      ?= nexus
PKG         := ./...
LINT        ?= golangci-lint

# Build version injected via -ldflags. Defaults to "dev" for local
# builds; the release workflow overrides this with the git tag (e.g.
# v1.0.0). Override locally with: make build VERSION=v1.2.3
VERSION     ?= dev
LDFLAGS     := -s -w -X main.version=$(VERSION)

.PHONY: help build run test test-race bench bench-short vet fmt lint tidy ci clean docker-build

help:
	@echo "Targets:"
	@echo "  build       - compile $(BINARY) into ./bin/"
	@echo "  run         - go run ./cmd/nexus"
	@echo "  test        - run unit tests"
	@echo "  test-race   - run unit tests with -race"
	@echo "  bench       - run all benchmarks with -benchmem -count=5"
	@echo "  bench-short - run benchmarks with -benchtime=100ms for CI"
	@echo "  vet         - go vet"
	@echo "  fmt         - gofmt -w (writes in place)"
	@echo "  lint        - golangci-lint run"
	@echo "  tidy        - go mod tidy"
	@echo "  ci          - vet + build + test + test-race + lint (what CI runs)"
	@echo "  docker-build - build the container image (smoke; needs Docker)"
	@echo "  clean       - remove ./bin/ and coverage files"

build:
	@mkdir -p bin
	$(GO) build -trimpath -ldflags="$(LDFLAGS)" -o bin/$(BINARY) ./cmd/nexus

run:
	$(GO) run ./cmd/nexus

test:
	$(GO) test $(PKG)

test-race:
	$(GO) test -race $(PKG)

# Benchmarks — see docs/BENCHMARKS.md for the baseline run that
# produced the reference numbers, and instructions for re-running on a
# new machine.
#
# `make bench` is the full pass (5x iterations per benchmark, suitable
# for local profiling). Use `make bench-short` on CI: -benchtime=100ms
# caps every benchmark at ~100ms so the whole suite runs in under 30s
# while still catching gross regressions.
BENCH_PACKAGES ?= $(PKG)

bench:
	$(GO) test -run='^$$' -bench=. -benchmem -count=5 -benchtime=1s $(BENCH_PACKAGES)

bench-short:
	$(GO) test -run='^$$' -bench=. -benchmem -benchtime=100ms $(BENCH_PACKAGES)

vet:
	$(GO) vet $(PKG)

fmt:
	$(GO) fmt $(PKG)

lint:
	$(LINT) run

tidy:
	$(GO) mod tidy
